THIS CRIMINAL PETITION IS FILED UNDER SECTION 482 OF CR.P.C., PRAYING TO QUASH THE FIR IN CR.NO.187/2023 OF JEEVAN BEEHANAGAR P.S., PENDING ON THE FILE OF 10TH A.C.M.M, COURT AT BENGALURU REGISTERED FOR THE OFFENCE P/U/S 506, 341, 34, 294, 323, 324 AND 351 OF IPC.

THESE PETITIONS, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER
The parties to the lis are all family members in a matrimonial dispute between the husband and the wife.

2. During the pendency of these petitions, the parties were referred to Bangalore Mediation Centre to explore the possibility of settlement, wherein the parties have settled the dispute before the Mediation.
One of the conditions of NC: 2024:KHC:26259 settlement is co-operation with the closure of the present proceedings.
The settlement is arrived at in M.C.No.3895 of 2022 between the parties.

The Memorandum of Settlement reads as follows:
"....1. The petitioner and R-2 were married to each other on 26.04.2019 at Janabhavan Shree Ramachandrapura Mutt, Peraje, Dakshina Kannada District and the same came to be registered before the Office of the Registrar Compulsory Registration of Marriage, Bantwal bearing Marriage Serial No.BNT- HM30-2019-20 dated: 30.04.2019.
2. Due to irreconcilable differences and incompatibility of temperaments, the parties have been living separately from 15.06.2022.
3. The parties herein state that they have a no children born to them from this wedlock.
4. The petitioner has agreed to pay a sum of Rs.24,00,000/- (Rupees Twenty Four Lakhs Only) to the 2nd respondent towards the claims of maintenance/permanent alimony in full and final settlement.

5. The petitioner and the R-2 state that they have entered into an elaborate agreement in MC No.3895/2022 which is pending on the file of I Addl. Family Court,
Smt Sushma Rani vs State Of Karnataka on 9 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109350989/
4 filed by the petitioner himself herein for a decree of a divorce.
III.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid agreement entered into between the parties, herein and in above mention MC NO.3895/2022 the parties pray that this Hon'ble Court be pleased to pass appropriate order in terms of this settlement agreement."

In the light of the settlement arrived at between the parties and the offences punishable being under Sections 498A and 506 of the IPC inter alia and not being against the State or Society, I deem it appropriate to accept the settlement and terminate the proceedings against the petitioners, in both the petitions.
4. For the aforesaid reasons, the following:
ORDER (
i) Criminal Petitions are disposed.

(ii) Both the FIRs in Crime No.187 of 2023 pending before the 10th ACMM.,
Bengaluru and in Crime No.152 of 2022 pending before the 6th ACMM, Bengaluru,
stand quashed.
